flow: Susceptible Humans->Removed Human logistic crowding loss
Exposed Humans->Removed Human logistic crowding loss

Susceptible Adult female vectors->Exposed Adult female vectors
Exposed Adult female vectors->Infectious Adult female vectors
param: λ Human population logistic growth rate
K_H Carrying capacity for human population (Rio de Janeiro State simulation value)
β Effective infectious bites delivered per vector per day (used as combined transmission factor in equations)
b Average biting rate per female mosquito per unit time (not separately identifiable from β in provided tables; set to 1.0 so β matches 'infectious bites per vector per day')
M Number of alternative hosts besides humans in the environment (reduces bites on humans via N_H+M)
α_H Progression rate from exposed humans to infectious humans (1 / human incubation time; 3 days used in simulations)
γ Recovery rate of infectious humans (1 / recovery time; 7 days used in simulations)
e_V Number of eggs laid per female mosquito per unit time
τ_1 Egg development rate to larva (1 / egg development time; 3 days)
τ_2 Larval development rate to pupa (1 / larval development time; 9 days)
τ_3 Pupal development rate to adult (1 / pupal development time; 3 days)
μ_2 Larval mortality rate (baseline, excluding density-dependent term)
μ_V Adult female mosquito mortality rate
q Proportion of females among emerging adult vectors
K_V Larval carrying capacity (Rio de Janeiro State simulation value)
κ Density-dependent larval mortality coefficient due to limited carrying capacity
α_V Progression rate from exposed adult vectors to infectious adult vectors (1 / vector incubation time; 10 days used in simulations)
